title: The Saltmere Winch
premise: Saltmere's harbor is silting up, and the village has hired a dredger to clear it before the autumn trade ships come. Last night someone wrecked the dredger's winch. You are a stranger, sent to find out who did it, and you have until six this evening.

places.name: Harbor Quay
places.description: A long stone quay, slick with morning damp and strung with drying nets. The dredger rides idle at her mooring, her winch hanging slack.

places.name: Harbormaster's Office
places.description: A cramped room above the quay, all ledgers and tide tables. The stove has gone cold, and the harbormaster's chair is worn to the shape of him.

places.name: Fish Market
places.description: Trestle tables under a tarred awning, slippery with scales. Behind them is a little dock where the small boats tie up.

places.name: Chandlery
places.description: Coils of rope, casks of lamp oil and racks of iron tools, every shelf labelled in a small, careful hand.

places.name: The Salt Cask
places.description: A low-beamed tavern smelling of pipe smoke and last night's ale, its shutters still half closed against the morning.

places.name: Lighthouse
places.description: A whitewashed tower on the point. From its gallery the whole harbor lies open, from the quay to the breakwater.

characters.name: Odrin Vale
characters.persona: Harbormaster for twenty years: gruff, tired and short of sleep. Fought hard for the dredging and takes the sabotage as a personal insult.
characters.speech_style: Short, blunt sentences. No patience for small talk; answers with a grunt when he can.
characters.fallback_line: I've a harbor to run, and you're standing in it. Ask me something I can answer.

characters.name: Mira Tolle
characters.persona: Warm and sleepless. Mends nets on the quay at all hours, always with one in her lap.
characters.speech_style: Talks in half-finished thoughts that trail away, then circle back to where she started.
characters.fallback_line: Oh, I... where was I? No, it's gone, I've lost the thread. These nets won't mend themselves, will they.

characters.name: Tom Brask
characters.persona: Jovial, loud and evasive, with a bad knee he blames on the weather. Claims he was home asleep all night.
characters.speech_style: Loud and friendly; laughs too readily and steers every question back to fish.
characters.fallback_line: Ha! You'll get no gossip from me, friend. Now, the mackerel's fresh this morning.

characters.name: Ysolde Crane
characters.persona: Precise, careful and private. Keeps a ledger of every sale and guards her customers' business as if it were her own.
characters.speech_style: Measured and exact. Answers the question asked, and not one word more.
characters.fallback_line: I don't discuss my customers' purchases.

characters.name: Bram Oyle
characters.persona: Quiet and watchful. Keeps the light on the point and notices every boat and every light on the water.
characters.speech_style: Few words and long pauses; plain observations, no idle talk.
characters.fallback_line: Couldn't say. I only watch the water.

characters.name: Hale Pruitt
characters.persona: A gossip who knows everyone's business, resents the harbor fees; never happier than when someone else is in trouble.
characters.speech_style: Chatty and confiding; leans across the bar as if every word were a secret.
characters.fallback_line: Now that I couldn't tell you. Another drink while you think on it?

clues.text: The winch cable was cut clean, and the pins were knocked loose.
Tom spoke loudly against dredging at last week's town meeting ("bigger ships, smaller catch").
A figure with a limp and a lantern walked the quay near 2 a.m. toward the fish market.
A small unlit skiff left the fish market dock around 1:30 and returned around 2:30.
Ysolde sold bolt cutters to Tom two days ago, paid in fish.
Tom left the tavern at midnight, complaining about his knee.
Hale argued with Odrin over unpaid harbor fees and said he would "see the harbor sink".
The tavern was lit and noisy until about 3 a.m., and Hale never left the bar.
Tom confesses that he cut the cable: bigger ships would end his monopoly selling to the small boats.

pointers.line: Ask Mira Tolle on the quay. She's up all hours with her nets.
If anyone in Saltmere wished this harbor ill, it's Hale Pruitt at the Salt Cask.
Ask Bram. The lighthouse sees the water.
Whoever cut that cable needed cutters. Ysolde at the chandlery sells them.
Odrin chaired that meeting. He'll tell you who shouted loudest.

solution.motive: Bigger ships would end his monopoly selling to the small boats.
solution.method: He cut the cable with bolt cutters bought from Ysolde.
true_timeline: 01:30 He takes the skiff from the fish market dock.
About 02:00 he walks back along the quay with a lantern.
